issues.problem: The phrase “each differing by more than 0.005 after rounding” does not specify a valid reproduction decision rule. Read literally, it requires k, d and both confidence limits all to differ before declaring failure. Thus, retaining k = 447 could prevent rejection even if the estimated effect were entirely different. Alternatively, “each” might mean that any discrepant quantity triggers failure, but that is not what the text clearly says.
issues.fix: State explicitly that reproduction fails if k is not exactly 447 OR if any one of the three continuous quantities fails its specified agreement criterion. Specify the rounding convention and what happens at a boundary.

issues.location: quote, test and fidelity: interpretation of “Refuted”
issues.problem: The proposed outcome conflates computational reproduction with refutation of the substantive claim. A discrepancy from the corrected table establishes a reproduction failure, not necessarily that choice architecture interventions do not promote behavior change. Conversely, exact reproduction of these selected-data estimates cannot establish the substantive claim against publication bias or other validity objections. The context recognizes this limitation, but the registered outcome still assigns the substantive label “Refuted” to a numerical discrepancy.
issues.fix: Register the computational claim that the specified analysis of the corrected data yields the specified estimates, with an outcome labelled reproduction success or failure. Keep the broader behavioral claim separate. If the protocol requires a refutation label, identify precisely which computational proposition is being refuted and explicitly prohibit interpreting that label as resolution of the broader effectiveness dispute.

issues.problem: The stated rationale uses 0.005 as the half-width of a two-decimal rounding interval, but the test applies that tolerance after rounding. These are different procedures. Once both values are rounded to two decimals, a discrepancy greater than 0.005 simply means that the displayed hundredths differ. The rule also does not say to how many decimals the rerun values are rounded.
issues.fix: Choose one procedure: compare rerun values rounded to two decimals with the published values, or compare unrounded rerun values with explicitly defined rounding intervals. Require the integer count to agree exactly rather than applying a decimal tolerance to it.

issues.problem: Requiring every domain confidence interval to lie wholly above zero makes insufficient precision a refutation condition. issues.location: test and data: executable analysis specification
issues.problem: The files are fingerprinted, but the item does not fully identify which outputs determine its verdict. issues.problem: The month-level interval from January 1982 through December 2021 gives more temporal precision than the cited publication-year range supplies.
